column3: The Hebrew names “the servant of the LORD” and repeats Moses’ name; BSB uses “His servant Moses” and later “Moses’ assistant.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “this Jordan” and “to them, to the sons of Israel”; BSB leaves “this” and “to them” implicit.
The Hebrew says “as I spoke to Moses”; BSB interprets the speaking as a promise.
The Hebrew says “this Lebanon,” repeats “river” before Euphrates, and describes the sunset; BSB omits “this,” names the river once, and uses “west.”
The Hebrew repeats ordinary negation for leaving and forsaking; BSB uses “never” for the first clause.
The Hebrew says that you will make “your way” prosper; BSB has “you will prosper” and supplies “in all you do.”
The Hebrew says to command the people and explicitly calls it “this Jordan”; BSB has “tell” and simply “the Jordan.”
The Hebrew uses collective singular names for the Reubenite and Gadite; BSB uses plural names.
The Hebrew describes giving rest as a current action and then says He has given the land; BSB puts both actions in the future.
The Hebrew says “beyond the Jordan”; BSB specifies “on this side of the Jordan.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “your brothers” before giving rest, while BSB uses “them” and names the brothers later. It describes “the rising of the sun,” rendered as “east.”
The Hebrew introduces the wish with “only”; BSB has “And.”
The Hebrew says “your mouth”; BSB interprets the image as “your order.”
